newsitem.title: UK: UK's Cook hails NATO-Russia agreement as positive.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cook hails NATO-Russia agreement as positive.

text.p: Britain's new foreign secretary Robin Cook on Tuesday hailed a new NATO-Russia agreement as a positive step which should not weaken the western alliance or threaten Moscow.
"It sets out a very bold, ambitious programme of joint co-operation," Cook told BBC radio. "There is no reason why it should weaken NATO,' he said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin are in Paris for the signing of the pact that lays the foundation of a new cooperative relationship between the former Cold War adversaries.
Cook, hailing the agreement, said: "I think the signals -- if we both use it and both put ourselves into making it work -- are very positive for a new relationship between Russia and the West."
Seeking to calm the fears of critics who oppose enlargement of NATO, he said: "There is no question of moving the troops forward into Poland and Hungary or any new member.
"Indeed today's agreement does say that we believe we can provide security in these countries without any substantial depoloyment of troops in their territory.

"That is another reason why the hardliners in Russia really ought to look at today's agreement and recognise that there is increasing confidence in security between us. This is opening the door to a new era of dialogue if they want to take it."
